tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Existence of a parametrix] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0246, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0247 ↗ def:chow-iii-ch23-parametrix ↗ lem:chow-iii-ch23-heat-error-derivatives 1. ch23:23.12\group Parametrix

Choose a smooth radial $\eta $ with $\eta =1$ on $[0,\operatorname {inj}(g)/4]$, $\eta =0$ on $[\operatorname {inj}(g)/2,\infty )$, bounded derivatives, and set \[ P_N(x,t;y,u):=\eta (d(x,y))H_N(x,t;y,u). \] For $N>n/2$, $P_N$ is a parametrix.
Proof

\sketch The support of $\eta $ lies inside the injectivity neighborhood, so $P_N$ is smooth. The product rule gives

\[ \Box _xP_N=\eta \Box _xH_N+(\Delta _x\eta )H_N+2\langle abla \eta , abla H_N angle . \]

Near the diagonal the first term tends to zero by Lemma 1; away from it every term is exponentially small. The same argument in the $y$ variable proves continuous extension. The Gaussian approximate-identity limit follows by normal coordinates and the fact that $\eta =1$ near the diagonal; symmetry gives the second limit.

□
